items.definition:
mother's husband (not biological father)
Her stepfather was very kind to her.

a snake-like fish
The fisherman caught a slippery eel in his net.

a small digital image or icon used to express an idea or emotion
She sent a smiling emoji to show her happiness.

mother (informal); madam (Irish/Scottish)
"Can I help you, mam?" the shop assistant asked.

orange juice (informal)
Would you like some OJ with your breakfast?

pajamas (informal)
He changed into his PJs before bed.

a vehicle for traveling over snow or ice
The children rode their sled down the snowy hill.

a dessert made with cheese
For dessert, I ordered a slice of strawberry cheesecake.

a bivalve mollusk
We dug for clams on the beach at low tide.

the amount of snow that falls
We had a heavy snowfall last night.

an instrument for measuring temperature
She used a thermometer to check her temperature.

a comfortable padded chair with arms
He relaxed in his favorite armchair by the fireplace.

a person who looks after children while their parents are out
We hired a babysitter for Saturday night.

a small square of rich chocolate cake, typically containing nuts
She baked a batch of delicious chocolate brownies.

a knitted jacket, typically buttoning down the front
She put on a warm cardigan because it was chilly.

a small bed with high barred sides for a baby or young child; a light portable bed
The baby slept soundly in its cot.

the globe of the eye
The doctor examined the patient's eyeball for any signs of injury.

a large vehicle for transporting goods by road (British English)
The lorry delivered the goods to the warehouse.

a boy attending school
The schoolboy carried a heavy backpack.

a person who sends something
The package did not have a return address for the sender.

a board with wheels for riding
He rode his skateboard down the street.

a vegetable with a large white flower head
I like to roast cauliflower with olive oil.

a large spotted cat known for its speed
The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

a cleaning substance
We ran out of laundry detergent.

the hard, flat, translucent covering on the end of a finger
She painted her fingernails bright red.

a person whose job is to extinguish fires
The brave fireman rescued the cat from the tree.

A person employed to look after a building.
The janitor cleaned the school hallways every evening.

A ball of ground meat, often mixed with breadcrumbs and seasonings.
She served spaghetti with large meatballs for dinner.

television (informal)
Let's watch some telly tonight.

a light box or container, typically made of cardboard or plastic.
Please buy a carton of milk from the store.

A two-wheeled motor vehicle.
He rode his motorbike through the winding country roads.

a loose, long-sleeved, collarless pullover
She wore a comfortable sweatshirt to the gym.

a powered flying vehicle with fixed wings
The aeroplane took off smoothly from the runway.

a dense, chewy bread roll, typically shaped like a doughnut
I had a cream cheese bagel for breakfast.

A person who drinks (especially alcohol)
He's a heavy drinker.

Dental floss; a type of thread
Don't forget to floss your teeth every day.

a person who sits for a specific purpose, e.g., babysitter
We hired a new sitter for the kids.

a ball of snow pressed together
The children had a snowball fight in the park.

a large spoon, used for serving or measuring
Add two tablespoons of sugar to the mixture.

a spring-flowering plant of the lily family, with large, cup-shaped flowers
The garden was full of colorful tulips.

a small, red, tart berry
We had cranberry sauce with our Thanksgiving turkey.

a dessert made with milk, eggs, and sugar
She poured warm custard over the apple pie.

a small fried cake of sweetened dough
He bought a box of doughnuts for breakfast.

grapefruit
I like to eat half a grapefruit for breakfast.

a person who cuts and styles hair
I have an appointment with my hairdresser tomorrow.

a fold of skin that covers and protects the eye
She gently closed her eyelids and fell asleep.

wood cut for burning
We gathered firewood for the campfire.

a piece of cloth or paper used at meals
Please put a napkin on your lap before you eat.

a figure made of snow
The children built a snowman in the garden.

a woman who is married to one's father but is not one's biological mother
Her stepmother was very kind to her.

a covering or outer layer
Please throw the candy wrapper in the bin.

a flat, rounded candy on a stick
The child happily licked his strawberry lollipop.

a soft, spongy confection
We roasted marshmallows over the campfire.

a member of a family of brass wind instruments
She learned to play the saxophone in high school.

A set of stairs
The old house had a grand stairway.

a dried grape
I like to add raisins to my oatmeal.

the activity of visiting places of interest in a particular location
We spent the day sightseeing in the city.

a large, thick-skinned African mammal
We saw a hippo swimming in the river at the zoo.

a tool for turning screws
He used a screwdriver to tighten the loose screw.

a substance applied to the body to prevent odor
He applied deodorant before leaving for work.

a short, curved hair growing from the edge of the eyelid
She had long, dark eyelashes.

a dish made with layers of pasta, sauce, and cheese
We had lasagna for dinner last night.

A shop where books are sold
I spent hours browsing in the old bookshop.

a person who goes on long walks in the countryside
The hiker enjoyed the scenic views from the mountain trail.
